faqs.question: What size should a Diwali quote image be for Instagram?
faqs.answer: 1080 × 1440 pixels, a 3:4 ratio, is the tallest feed size Instagram keeps uncropped, according to its help centre as read in October 2026. Anything between 1.91:1 and 3:4 at 1080 pixels wide keeps its resolution; a Story uses a separate 1080 × 1920 canvas.

faqs.question: Is 4:5 still okay for an Instagram quote post?
faqs.answer: Yes. A 1080 × 1350 image sits inside Instagram's supported range, so it posts uncropped. It simply gives the quote 90 fewer pixels of height than a 3:4 canvas.

faqs.question: How big should the text be on a quote graphic?
faqs.answer: On a 1080-pixel-wide canvas, start at about 90 to 110 px for a single short line and 64 to 80 px for two lines. Those are our working figures; the real test is reading it on your phone at arm's length without zooming.

faqs.question: Which Diwali colours are readable for text?
faqs.answer: Maroon on cream (9.58:1), gold on maroon (6.12:1) and white on near-black (17.40:1) all clear the WCAG 2.2 minimum of 4.5:1. Saffron on white (2.13:1) and gold on cream (1.56:1) fail even the 3:1 large-text floor.

faqs.question: What should I write in the alt text for a Diwali quote image?
faqs.answer: Write the quote itself, word for word, as the W3C's images-of-text tutorial advises. Add a short description of the picture only if it adds meaning, and skip the font, colours and effects.

faqs.question: Should the quote also go in my caption?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under WCAG 1.4.5, an image of text shown with the same words as real text meets the criterion, and on Instagram that real text is the caption. Put the quote on the first line and any hashtags after it.

faqs.question: Can I put a Hindi quote on an Instagram graphic?
faqs.answer: Yes. Set the Devanagari about 10% larger than you would an English line, and put the Roman transliteration and English meaning in the caption. The five Hindi lines on this page are written to be used that way.

faqs.question: When should I post Diwali quotes in 2027?
faqs.answer: Lakshmi Puja is Friday 29 October 2027, with Dhanteras on 27 October and Bhai Dooj on 31 October. Post lamp quotes on the evening of the 29th and make the graphics a day or two before.

faqs.question: Do I need to credit these quotes?
faqs.answer: No. All 20 were written for this page rather than collected from other lists, so you can post them under your own name.

faqs.question: Can a SubhSandesh Diwali card go on my Instagram Story?
faqs.answer: Its final Shubh Deepavali card can be saved as a 1080 × 1920 image, which is Story size. The full interactive page opens from a private link, so send that link to the one person it is meant for.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Diwali Quotes for Instagram, Laid Out to Read on a Phone

The Diwali quotes for Instagram that get read are short enough to sit large on a 1080 × 1440 pixel canvas, are set at a contrast of at least 4.5:1, and are repeated word for word in the alt text and caption. Below are 20 original quotes written to fit that method. Design for a phone: on SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages are opened on a phone and 48.4% of views come from a touch device (measured 24 September 2026).

Canvas sizes, lettering, alt text and timing for Diwali 2027 (Friday 29 October) follow the quotes. The last section says when a graphic is the wrong format.

## What makes a Diwali quote work as an Instagram graphic?

A Diwali quote graphic is an image of text: a festival line set over a colour or photo and posted as a picture. The W3C's [Understanding document for WCAG 1.4.5, Images of Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text.html), names the catch in one line: people cannot alter how text looks in images.

So the quote must be legible without zooming, and the same words must also exist as real text. That is why these 20 quotes are grouped by how much fits the frame, not by mood.

## 20 original Diwali quotes, sorted by how much fits the frame

Every line was written for this page. Each group gives a layout, a starting font size on a 1080-pixel-wide canvas and a margin, our working figures rather than an Instagram rule.

### 1. Under ten words, for a single-line graphic

Set one centred line on a plain background at about 90 to 110 px. Keep 100 px clear on every edge.

- Darkness never wins against one stubborn wick.
- Light the lamp you were waiting for.
- Tonight even the balcony has a halo.
- Every wick on this ledge was lit by hand.
- Same lamps as last year, brighter people around them.

### 2. Two lines, for a portrait feed post

Put the first line in the upper third of a 3:4 canvas and the second in the lower third, at about 64 to 80 px. Break exactly at the slash; a quote split mid-thought reads as two claims.

- We swept every corner for Lakshmi. / We left one lamp on for whoever gets home late.
- The oil runs out by morning. / The warmth lasts until next Kartik.
- Bring the old grudge to the doorstep. / Leave it where the rangoli ends.
- The moon took the night off. / We hung forty small ones along the railing.
- Not every light is loud. / Some just stay lit beside you all night.

### 3. Three beats, for a carousel

Each slash marks a new slide, one short line per slide at about 70 to 90 px. Keep every slide on the same canvas and margins so the text does not jump between swipes.

- Before the lamps, the cleaning. / Before the sweets, the queue at the halwai. / Before the night, all of us, home at last.
- The rangoli took four hours. / The dog crossed it in four seconds. / We kept the paw prints.
- Thirteen diyas along the boundary wall. / One kept going out. / Nani said that one is still learning.
- Dhanteras, something new. / Choti Diwali, something swept. / Lakshmi Puja, everything lit.
- Last Diwali you were a video call. / This year you are lighting the lamp next to mine.

### 4. Hindi lines, with transliteration and meaning

Devanagari carries matras above and below the headline, so give it about 10% more size than English. Keep the transliteration and meaning for the caption.

- दीया छोटा है, उजाला बड़ा। (Diya chhota hai, ujaala bada.) The lamp is small; its light is not.
- अमावस की रात, फिर भी कोई कोना अँधेरा नहीं। (Amaavas ki raat, phir bhi koi kona andhera nahin.) A moonless night, yet not one corner is dark.
- मिठाई बाँटो, हिसाब नहीं। (Mithai baanto, hisaab nahin.) Share the sweets, not the score.
- जो दूर हैं, उनके नाम का भी एक दीया। (Jo door hain, unke naam ka bhi ek diya.) One lamp, too, in the name of those far away.
- घर साफ़, मन हल्का, दरवाज़ा खुला। (Ghar saaf, man halka, darwaaza khula.) A clean house, a light heart, an open door.

## The canvas sizes Instagram keeps uncropped, as of October 2026

Instagram's [help page on image resolution](https://help.instagram.com/1631821640426723), read on 22 October 2026, says a photo between 320 and 1080 pixels wide keeps its original resolution when its aspect ratio sits between 1.91:1 and 3:4. At 1080 pixels wide that is a height of 566 to 1440 pixels; anything outside that range is cropped.

So the tallest feed graphic Instagram leaves alone is 1080 × 1440. Much advice still names 4:5 (1080 × 1350) as the limit; it posts uncropped too, but 3:4 gives a quote 90 more pixels.

A Story is a separate 1080 × 1920 canvas, the size SubhSandesh's Diwali card saves at. We keep a 250 px band clear at the top and bottom for the profile name and reply bar, our working margin rather than an Instagram figure.

## How big and how dark should the words be?

WCAG 2.2, the [W3C Recommendation dated 12 December 2024](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), asks for a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for text and images of text, and 3:1 for large-scale text of at least 18 point or 14 point bold. It adds that extraordinarily thin strokes are harder to read at lower contrast, so avoid hairline scripts.

Festive palettes often fail. We measured common Diwali pairs with the WCAG formula: maroon #7A1F1F on cream #FFF6E5 is 9.58:1, gold #F2C14E on that maroon is 6.12:1, and white on near-black #1A1A1A is 17.40:1. Saffron #FF9933 on white is 2.13:1 and gold on cream is 1.56:1, so both fail even the 3:1 large-text floor.

Size matters as much as colour. A [2023 systematic review of 28 studies by Muhamad and Amali](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10512131) found users preferred high luminance contrast and positive polarity, meaning dark text on a light background, and favoured larger fonts on smartphones but smaller ones on desktops and laptops.

Even SubhSandesh's pages, which open in a browser rather than an app, get 48.3% of their views on a phone. Run three checks before posting.

- Hold your phone at arm's length; if you need to zoom, the type is too small.
- Run the two colours through a WCAG contrast checker; below 4.5:1, darken one of them.
- Use a heavier weight for the main line, with decorative lettering on one word at most.

## Alt text and caption: putting the quote into words twice

The W3C's [tutorial on images of text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/textual/) says the text alternative for an image of text must contain the same text presented in the image. Decorative effects such as stylised lettering or shadows are not described.

So the alt text is the quote itself, plus a phrase about the picture only when it adds something: "Light the lamp you were waiting for. Text over a single clay diya on a dark windowsill." Instagram lets you replace its automatic alt text with your own, before or after posting.

The WCAG 1.4.5 document adds that an image of text shown alongside the same words as real text meets the criterion. On Instagram that real text is your caption, so paste the quote as its first line, with any transliteration and meaning below.

## Feed post, carousel, Story or a Diwali page: compared

The five formats differ in canvas, type size and where the words live as real text. Canvases come from Instagram's help page and SubhSandesh's template; type sizes are our working figures.

| Format | Canvas | Starting font size | Where the quote also exists as real text |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single-line feed graphic | 1080 × 1440 px (3:4), uncropped | 90–110 px | Alt text and first caption line |
| Two-line portrait post | 1080 × 1440 px or 1080 × 1350 px (4:5) | 64–80 px | Alt text and first caption line |
| Carousel, one line per slide | 1080 × 1440 px on every slide | 70–90 px | Alt text per slide, full quote in caption |
| Story graphic | 1080 × 1920 px, 250 px bands kept clear | 80–100 px | None; Stories have no caption |
| SubhSandesh Diwali card | Ends on a card saved at 1080 × 1920 px | Set by the template | The whole page is browser text |

The takeaway: the 3:4 feed post gives a quote the most room Instagram allows without cropping. The caption then carries the words for everyone else.

## When to post in 2027, and when a graphic is the wrong format

Diwali 2027 runs from Dhanteras on Wednesday 27 October to Bhai Dooj on Sunday 31 October, with Lakshmi Puja on Friday 29 October. Post cleaning and shopping quotes on the 27th or 28th, and lamp lines on the evening of the 29th.

Make the graphics early. SubhSandesh has no Diwali creation data yet, but in its Raksha Bandhan 2026 data, the nearest festival analogue and a small sample of n = 89 pages, 49.4% were built on the festival day itself.

A public quote graphic speaks to everyone who follows you, which makes it the wrong place for a line meant for one person. For a parent in another city or a partner away this year, SubhSandesh's [interactive Diwali card with wish diyas and a liffafa letter](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-diwali) puts your words on a diya tag, a row of wish diyas and a letter in a shagun liffafa. It opens from a private link in any browser with no app or account, ending on a Shubh Deepavali card they can save at Story size.

It is a one-person greeting page, not a design tool, and a relative who rarely uses a smartphone is better served by the quote printed on a card in the mithai box. For a long quote, [The Last Piece photo jigsaw](https://subhsandesh.in/photo-puzzle) reveals one line of your letter per piece placed; it is not a Diwali template, but it beats a crowded graphic.

## Sources

- W3C, [Understanding SC 1.4.5: Images of Text](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/images-of-text.html), undated.
- W3C, [WCAG 2.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/), Recommendation, 12 December 2024.
- W3C WAI, [Images of Text tutorial](https://www.w3.org/WAI/tutorials/images/textual/), undated.
- Instagram Help Centre, [Image resolution of photos you share on Instagram](https://help.instagram.com/1631821640426723), undated.
- Muhamad and Amali, [Digital Display Preference of Electronic Gadgets for Visual Comfort](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC10512131), Iranian Journal of Public Health, August 2023.
